answer.generated: Cache performance is closely related to the virtual memory hierarchy because the intermediate level of real memory, which separates virtual and physical memory, affects how cache coherence is maintained across different memory tiers. In many RISC architectures, the virtual memory architecture uses TLB structures to map virtual memory to real memory, enabling efficient translation and caching. This mapping allows the processor to access physical memory through the intermediate real memory layer, optimizing both cache performance and overall system performance by reducing TLB misses.
